arm-A.title: Trinity's capture and breakout in Room 303
arm-A.summary: Four officers breach Room 303 in the fire-gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity at gunpoint; she complies with deliberate slowness, paying them the image of a cornered woman to buy the seconds she needs. Outside, three Agents strip the Lieutenant of his operation, correcting him that his two units are already dead while he insists his men are winning. Back in the room, the moment the Big Cop reaches to cuff her, Trinity moves faster than the squad can track: she disarms and kills all four cops and stands alone over the bodies, a single curse escaping her.
arm-A.action: The raid succeeds on paper — Trinity is cornered and complies — but her obedience is only timing, the first move of a trap. The trigger is touch, not threat: the instant the Big Cop's cuffs reach for her, she breaks the arrest and turns the squad into corpses. Meanwhile the Agents arrive and, without firing a shot, declare the police effort already a failure, their calm resting on the fact that they already know the officers are dead.

arm-B.title: Trinity's capture turns into a massacre
arm-B.summary: Four cops breach Room 303 in the fire-gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity at gunpoint; she raises her hands behind her head in apparent surrender. Outside, the Lieutenant brags that his units are bringing down 'one little girl' while Agent Smith tells him those men are already dead. Back inside, the moment the Big Cop reaches with the cuffs, Trinity moves inhumanly fast: she shatters his nose and hurls him across the room into another cop, killing them both, snatches a gun, twists it, and fires. When the gunfire ends, one flashlight rocks slowly to a stop over the dead and Trinity is the only one standing, unhurt. She lets slip a single 'Shit.' Outside, Smith turns and heads into the hotel on Smith's nod, leaving the defiant, disbelieving Lieutenant behind.
arm-B.action: The raid on Room 303 inverts in a single instant. Trinity's surrender in the room is a choice, not a defeat: she lets the squad believe the arrest is routine, then converts the first physical contact — the Big Cop's cuffs reaching for her — into the opening of her violence. She breaks the perimeter, turns the cops' own momentum and weapons against them, and by the end has wiped out the armed, outnumbering squad, standing alone over the dead as the victor rather than the captive. Outside the hotel, the Agents already know the outcome and move to seize the operation while the Lieutenant, still believing his men are succeeding, rages against them in denial.

arm-A.title: Trinity's flight to the exit phone
arm-A.summary: Trinity's planned exit collapses when Morpheus tells her the traced hardline is dead and Agents are on site, so she commits to a phone at Wells and Lake. She breaks from the hall moments before Agent Brown and a police unit enter, is forced up the fire escape when Agent Smith holds the alley below, and runs the rooftops where she clears an impossible 40-foot gap — a leap Agent Brown then duplicates with the same unnatural grace, shattering the cops' model of physics and revealing the pursuers break the world's rules too. She hurls herself across a 50-foot chasm into a dark building, crashes through a window onto a back stairwell, and, broken and bleeding, gets up and keeps moving. Racing a garbage truck on the street below, she reaches the ringing phone booth and answers it an instant before the truck pulverizes it, gone before the Agents can take her — while Smith, Jones, and Brown confirm the informant is real and that they now have the next target's name, and Smith almost smiles at the prospect of running a search.
arm-A.action: Trinity re-centers on Morpheus's order and commits to the run, driving herself through an impossible rooftop gap, a window, and a stairwell crash, absorbing real injury without letting it stop her, and answers the phone a split-second before the truck destroys the booth. Morpheus holds compressed alarm under a hard shell of command, and his 'You can make it' is an assertion of confidence in Trinity, not a guess. The traced hardline fails, converting a secured victory over the police into a desperate flight through hall, fire escape, rooftops, a 50-foot dive, and a stairwell crash until the street becomes a kill box. The Wells and Lake phone organizes the entire flight as the one fixed point Trinity commits to. Agent Brown duplicates Trinity's impossible leap with unnatural grace, revealing himself as a superhuman threat equal to her. Agent Smith, frustrated that Trinity escaped, learns from Brown that the informant is real and they have the next target's name, and almost smiles at the prospect of running a search. The rooftop cops' confident certainty curdles into uncomprehending fear as her impossible leap and Brown's exact duplication shatter their ordinary model of physics. Agent Jones reports the search already begun before the order is given, and the collective trades one failure for a colder victory as their surveillance turns toward the named quarry.

arm-B.summary: Morpheus tells Trinity the traced hardline is cut and she must reach the Wells and Lake phone instead. She bolts through a hall where Agent Brown appears and out a broken window onto the fire escape, only to find Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, forcing her up onto the roof. She runs the rooftops with cold grace while the cops flounder and Brown duplicates her leap across the 40-foot gap, then she dives through a lit window, crashes down a stairwell, and races the garbage truck to the booth. arm-A.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-A.summary: Alone in his technology-crammed apartment, Neo is jolted from sleep by his own PC typing messages at him that end with a real knock answering the screen, leaving him unable to tell whether he was awake or dreaming. He still closes a disk-for-cash deal with Choi through his chained, multi-locked door, but the visit leaves him hollowed by a returning sense of unrealness, and when Dujour proposes taking him out he refuses until he spots a small white rabbit pin on her jacket, at which the room seems to tilt and he agrees. At a smoke-filled gathering of people dressed in black, Trinity walks straight up to him, names herself as the hacker who was on his computer, warns him that he is in danger and being watched, and reframes his sleepless solitude as a search for a hidden figure and an answer no one can be told. Pressing close in the deafening music, she withholds the substance and instead gives him the question, which he finally voices aloud before she melts back into the crowd, leaving him with the promise that the answer is out there and will find him.
arm-A.action: Neo is woken at his PC by messages that type themselves on his screen and end with a knock that answers the last line, cracking his cause-and-effect certainty and blurring the machine into the real. He performs normalcy, opening his series of locks and chain to complete a disk-for-cash deal with Choi, then is left hollowed by a recurring wave of unrealness. He refuses Dujour's offer to go out until the white rabbit pin on her jacket flips him into motion, and he arrives at the party out of place, beer in hand. Trinity approaches, names herself as the one who was on his computer, warns him he is being watched and in danger, and turns his private, sleepless obsession into a directed search, pressing close in the loud music until he voices What is the Matrix? and is told the answer can only be seen, not explained. She then withdraws into the shifting crowd, leaving him alone with the question and the promise that the answer will find him.

arm-B.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-B.summary: Alone in his apartment, Neo is woken by his own screen typing messages that name him and command him to follow a white rabbit; a real knock answers the last line, and a visit from a drug buyer ends with him shaken and unable to trust cause and effect. When he spots a small white rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket, his resolve flips and he abandons his refusal to go out. Drawn to a crowded, black-clad gathering, he is met by name by Trinity, who confirms she was on his computer, warns him that he is in danger and being watched, reframes his sleepless solitude as the mark of a seeker, and presses her body to his as she tells him the answer he chases cannot be told but must be seen.
arm-B.action: Neo voices the question 'What is the Matrix?' aloud and is told the answer is out there, looking for him, before Trinity melts into the crowd and a rising sound closes over him.

arm-A.title: Neo's ordinary life reasserts itself
arm-A.summary: The alarm drags Neo awake at 9:15 A.M. in his own apartment, and he reacts with alarmed cursing at the time. An establishing shot names the destination as the downtown headquarters of Meta CorTechs, a software development firm. There, Rhineheart lectures him without looking up from his computer, accusing him of a problem with authority and demanding conformity as part of a whole, then delivers an ultimatum: be on time from this day forth or find another job. Neo, who has spent the exchange watching the window cleaners outside, answers with crisp deference — 'Yes, Mr. Rhineheart. Perfectly clear.' The vast, destabilizing pull of the night before collapses back into the mundane mechanics of a job he is about to lose.
arm-A.action: Neo is jolted from sleep by the alarm at 9:15 A.M. and reacts with alarmed cursing. arm-B.title: Neo's failed escape from Meta CorTechs
arm-B.summary: Across four linked beats, Neo's ordinary life is breached and then collapses. Waking late and alarmed, he endures Rhineheart's ultimatum with detached, surface-level compliance. A delivered phone connects him to Morpheus, who warns that 'they' are coming; Neo watches the Agents and cops close in, then obeys a turn-by-turn escape through the cubicle maze. Cornered in an empty office, he is told to cross a scaffold to the roof, commits to the ledge, but his nerve breaks when the wind hits and he climbs back inside at the moment a cop opens the door.
arm-B.action: The event converts Neo from a self-contained hacker into a hunted fugitive who must trust an unseen guide, and it does so by stripping away every layer of his ordinary world in sequence — sleep, job, anonymity, and finally his one escape route. The through-line is the transfer of agency: he stops questioning and starts obeying, yet that very obedience cannot carry him across the ledge, because his terror of the height drives him back inside toward the capture he cannot yet see at the door. His failure at the physical test is what delivers him into enemy hands.

arm-A.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
arm-A.summary: A softpak delivers a ringing phone to Neo's cubicle and Morpheus guides him through the raid, but the escape stalls at a window ledge and ends when the Agents take him into custody, which Trinity sees from outside.
arm-A.action: A Federal Express Guy delivers a softpak to Neo at his cubicle; inside is a cellular phone that rings the moment Neo holds it, and Morpheus warns that forces are closing in. Neo peeks over the partition and spots Agent Smith, Agent Brown and Agent Jones guiding a cluster of officers, while a female employee points out his cubicle. Following Morpheus's commands, Neo lunges into the empty cubicle across the hall, hides in a corner while the Agents search his own, then rolls out and sneaks down he moves down the line until he reaches the first office on the left side. Alone in that office, he opens a window onto a scaffold and a ledge, argues that the climb is impossible, then commits and climbs out onto the ledge anyway; a blast of wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone and watches it fall, and his nerve breaks so he climbs back inside just as a cop opens the door. Outside the skyscraper, the Agents lead a handcuffed Neo through the revolving doors and force him into a dark sedan while Trinity, watching from her motorcycle, sees him taken in her rearview mirror.

arm-B.title: Neo's failed escape from Meta CorTechs
arm-B.summary: Across four linked beats, Neo's ordinary life is breached and then collapses. Waking late and alarmed, he endures Rhineheart's ultimatum with detached, surface-level compliance. A delivered phone connects him to Morpheus, who warns that 'they' are coming; Neo watches the Agents and cops close in, then obeys a turn-by-turn escape through the cubicle maze. Cornered in an empty office, he is told to cross a scaffold to the roof, commits to the ledge, but his nerve breaks when the wind hits and he climbs back inside at the moment a cop opens the door.
arm-B.action: The event converts Neo from a self-contained hacker into a hunted fugitive who must trust an unseen guide, and it does so by stripping away every layer of his ordinary world in sequence — sleep, job, anonymity, and finally his one escape route. The through-line is the transfer of agency: he stops questioning and starts obeying, yet that very obedience cannot carry him across the ledge, because his terror of the height drives him back inside toward the capture he cannot yet see at the door. His failure at the physical test is what delivers him into enemy hands.

arm-A.title: Neo is taken and interrogated by the Agents
arm-A.summary: The Agents drag a handcuffed Neo out of the skyscraper and into a dark sedan while Trinity, watching from her motorcycle, catches the capture in her rearview mirror and reacts with dismay. In the interrogation room, Agent Smith lays out Neo's two lives from a manila file labeled 'Anderson, Thomas A.' and offers to erase his crimes in exchange for help hunting Morpheus. arm-B.title: Neo is interrogated and implanted
arm-B.summary: In a white interrogation room, Agent Smith reads Neo the contents of his file and offers to wipe his crimes clean in exchange for Morpheus's location. Neo refuses with contempt, gives Smith the finger, and demands a phone call. When Smith asks what good a call is if he cannot speak, Neo's lips meld together until his mouth is gone. Neo lunges for the door; the standing Agents pin him to the chair and tear open his shirt, and Smith drives a fiber-optic tap that has become a living insect-worm creature into his navel, where it burrows inside him as he panics and struggles.
arm-B.action: The scene opens on Neo seated whole-bodied and defiant in the room. Smith sits across from him, lays down the manila file labeled "Anderson, Thomas A.", and runs through Neo's two lives before offering to wipe the slate clean for Morpheus. Neo rejects the bargain, insults Smith, and demands his phone call. Smith removes his sunglasses to show ice-blue eyes and asks what use a call is if Neo cannot speak; Neo's lips fuse smooth. Neo lunges for the door, the standing Agents seize and hold him down while Smith rips his shirt open, and Smith withdraws a fiber-optic wire that animates into a living creature and drives it into Neo's navel, where it burrows in as Neo struggles helplessly.

arm-B.title: Neo chooses to meet Morpheus and is taken by the crew
arm-B.summary: A detained suspect who still believes he can assert his rights is pulled by a ringing phone into a brief, tapped conversation with Morpheus, who names him 'the One' and tells him the danger is himself, then extracts a single 'Yes' before directing him to the Adams Street bridge. On the rain-soaked bridge, Trinity pulls up and orders him into the car. Inside, Switch holds him at gunpoint and demands he strip for an unknown device while Apoc drives; Neo resists and opens the door to flee, but Trinity reframes the restraint as protection 'from you' and grounds her appeal in the road he already knows, and Switch stops the car to end all negotiation with an ultimatum.
arm-B.action: He bolts upright screaming, checks his mouth and stomach to confirm they are normal, then the ringing phone 'almost stops his heart.' His only lines are 'The Agents —', 'What the hell is happening to me?', and the hesitant '... Yes,' after which he shuts his eyes, uncertain about what he has just done.
